items.summary: Unit 5 summary: dates, months, greetings, presents, clothes, and numbers.
Review game classifying vocabulary: colours, animals, clothes, family, and odd-one-out puzzles.
Fill-in exercises on the French calendar, possessive adjectives, presents, and verbs avoir/être.
Weather map of France: true/false statements and temperature descriptions.
Listening comprehension on weather forecasts plus conversation and reading practice.
Seasons of the year: identifying seasons and completing weather description sentences.
Reading about French regional climates and writing about your own local weather.
Listening and correcting statements about who plays which sport.
Practising the verb jouer: choosing and completing correct conjugations for sports.
Comic strip about a cat chasing a mouse, with true/false comprehension questions.
Matching people to holiday activities using regular -er verbs, plus BD comic reading.
Reading about a naughty little brother, plus a lazy-family comic strip fill-in.
Fill-in verb forms and listening interviews about weekend activities and interests.
Reading about France's science festival and proposing weather-based activities.
Phone conversations and postcard writing about weather and activities.
Practising questions and answers about weekend free-time activities.
Unit 6 vocabulary summary: weather, seasons, -er verbs, and sports.
Comic story about a new student misunderstood by classmates at school.
Comprehension questions on the new-student story, plus a seasons song and a comic.
Introducing La Rochelle: matching descriptive sentences about the town to photos.
Vocabulary translation for La Rochelle's town features and day-of-week routines.
Town vocabulary: matching, listening, and fill-in exercises on amenities and adjectives.
Reading about La Rochelle's bike scheme and completing postcards about a visit.
Asking for directions in town via listening, questions, and a true/false story.
Direction-giving practice: listening, signpost fill-ins, and matching responses.
Choosing destinations in town using au/à la/aux prepositions.
Prepositions of place: true/false about a street scene and fill-in cartoon prompts.
Describing your town: vocabulary sorting, listening, and il y a / il n'y a pas de fill-ins.
Memory game and fill-in text about town amenities plus personal writing.
Fill-in exercises with the verb aller about who goes where.
